newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds calm, brace for volatile week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds calm, brace for volatile week.

text.p: *Australian bonds finished slightly weaker in a relatively subdued session as the market braced itself for what could prove to be another volatile trading week.
The Australian debt market ended slightly weaker in a relatively subdued session as it braced itself for what could prove to be another volatile trading week.

Traders noted some local profit-taking after the market had held its ground against a further weakening in U.S. Treasuries on Thursday, but the day's action was largely put down to pre-weekend and end of month squaring.
"We've seen very little today. I think the market wanted a day off after a wild week, and it got it. But next week could prove to be another bruiser," one trader said.

The market had attracted strong overseas interest in after-hours trading with yields becoming attractive after this week's generally weaker trend and as worries over a blowout in wages growth proved premature from data seen this week.
Next week sees an avalanche of data, including fourth quarter GDP, but interest could focus on the more up-to-date figures for retail trade and building approvals for January.

The end of next week also sees the key U.S. non-farm payrolls report, but the main focus for the U.S. and markets globally will be the second leg of Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday.

The local market's lack of conviction on its direction saw it give up some of its initial tightening against the dollar bloc, although margins remain well below this week's highs. The local profit-taking largely centred on the short-end, causing the yield curve to flatten slightly.
